subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a first-class distributed agent runtime/control-plane split in core, and which bounded phase should own the next implementation?
rationale: The request crosses core gateway, agent runtime, protocol, config, session state, channel delivery, and security boundaries; automation can verify it is not implemented, but cannot choose the permanent architecture or acceptable upgrade/security tradeoffs.

options.title: Keep RFC and sponsor Phase 0/1
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella, then require a maintainer-owned design for per-agent lifecycle/runtime protocol before accepting implementation slices.

options.title: Narrow to subagent execution backends
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and related PRs as the immediate path, leaving full gateway/control-plane separation deferred.

options.title: Close as out of current scope
options.body: Defer distributed runtime as too heavy for current OpenClaw core and ask for external deployment/plugin experiments until maintainers reopen the direction.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC and sponsor Phase 0/1
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella, then require a maintainer-owned design for per-agent lifecycle/runtime protocol before accepting implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the open worker-runtime experiment and recent adjacent runtime work, so he is the best available owner for the product-direction call.
